recipes.name: Chef John's Beans and Greens
ingredients_raw: salt and ground black pepper to taste

steps.text: Heat 2 tablespoons olive oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Add garlic; cook and stir until bubbling and sizzling, about 20 seconds. Pour in chicken broth and bring to a boil. Cook until liquid is reduced by half, 6 to 8 minutes. Stir in a pinch of red pepper flakes.

Stir in cannellini beans and bring to a boil. Cook until you can see the tops of the beans just below the surface of the liquid, 6 to 8 minutes. Stir in anchovy fillet, oregano, and lemon zest; simmer for 3 minutes.

Add escarole and reduce the heat to low. Cook and stir until escarole wilts, about 5 minutes. Season with salt and pepper, then drizzle with extra-virgin olive oil and add another pinch of red pepper flakes.

raw_recipe.headline: Chef John's Beans and Greens
raw_recipe.description: Chef John's beans and greens recipe is nutritious and comforting with creamy cannellini beans cooked in a flavorful broth with wilted escarole.

review.reviewBody: Excellent recipe as is. I chopped up 4 slices of bacon and sauted them until light brown. Used the rendered fat with less olive oil to saute the garlic and 1 chopped onion. At the end I added 1.5 tbsp. red wine vinegar and 2 tsp. sugar.
I can’t find canned cannellini in my area so I soaked and InstantPot-ed a pound of dry cannellini and proceeded from there. Nice, basic but versatile recipe. Thanks, Chef John!

Chef John I've enjoyed playing with this recipe! This time, I rendered nitrate free bacon. After removing the bacon from the pan, I removed the fatty parts and chopped the lean pieces to add later. I sauteed 1 yellow onion, 1 tsp curry powder and the garlic in the fat. Once the onions were caramelized, I added Trader Joe's low sodium vegetable stock, seasonings and liquid smoke. After reducing per your recipe, I added the beans, a can of Glory seasoned collard greens I had on hand and some leftover (cooked) turkey meatballs. The chopped bacon went into the pot in the final few minutes. Yum! Talk about amazing flavor and pretty healthy to boot.

I used instant pot- added 1 onion chopped and sauteed with garlic in oil in instant pot. Added the rest of ingredients and set for 5 minutes of pressure cooking. Immediately vented - family loves, loves loves this- me too!

I’ve never heard of this dish, so I’ve nothing to compare it to. We’ve recently been eating vegetarian and this recipe spoke to me. I followed the recipe as is, with a few minor tweaks: I used veggie stock, added some baby spinach, and had to use rolled anchovies as that’s all the store had. They’re actually my only issue with the dish. I love anchovies and the umami they add to a dish, but I did not care for them in this dish. When I make this again, I’ll nix the anchovies, increase the salt a touch, and include some of the bean liquid to help make up for the lost umami. I think I’ll also add some diced leeks or shallots and increase the greens. All in all, a winner; thanks, Chef John!

I've made this countless times, with whatever greens we have on hand. Escarole or baby bok choy give the most authentic results but it's delicious with everything I've used. My daughters are vegan so we leave out the anchovy (add some salt) and use Better than Bouillon. Sometimes, I'll add extra broth to make it soupier, if I'm in the mood...but basically this recipe is perfect.

I had some hot sausage already cooked in the fridge, so I added that at the start before garlic. Added raw fennel and raw cherry tomatoes on top because I had a lot extra. Also served with Cheesy Garlic bread or Warm bread stuffed with olive tapenade.

I made this tonight and it turned out so good. I only wish I had my mom’s recipe, but this turned out so well! The only thing is I used parsley instead of oregano, I used vegetable broth instead of chicken, added a little bit of chopped onion and omitted the anchovy.

Loved the recipe but also love to add some of my own ingredients from time to time. I personally love Italian Sausage with my greens and beans so I skinned and crumbled/sauteed ~ 1/2# sausage first, removed it then left the drippings in the pot. I eyeballed about how much additional olive oil I'd need to get to 2 TBSP. From there I followed the recipe EXCEPT added some leftover white wine (sweet, Moscato, ~ 1/2 cup) to the chicken stock before reducing by 1/2. I followed the recipe to the "T" from there and added the sausage back to the pot to simmer before adding the greens. LOVED IT!!!

Delicious!! I am vegetarian, so no anchovy, but I substituted a strip of kombu seaweed for a salty/fishy taste, and it worked great! I added it in the same step as the anchovy was called for in the recipe, and removed it after the escarole was almost done wilting. (I also added some diced onion in the first step.) It was fast, filling and nutritious!! I will make this again, for sure.

I didn't add the anchovy, oregano or lemon zest. I like old fashion Italian greens and beans. Reduced the chicken broth to just 2 cups. Sauted the beans in 5 tbsp EVOO with 6 cloves or more of chopped garlic. Added in the part of the broth, brought that to a simmer then added the escarole a little more EVOO and chopped garlic and the rest of the broth, 2 pinches of red pepper flakes, salt and pepper. I also always have end pieces of the rind from Romano or parmigiano cheese so put that in while on simmer for the greens to finish cooking. This was AWESOME!!
Worst soup I've ever made
its a good way to eat beans and spice them up I liked it we will be cooking this one once a week

I absolutely love everything about this recipe and haven’t changed a thing in the 5 or 6 times I’ve made it. It’s just absolutely perfect! But for some reason, it’s very difficult to find escarole, so i’ve used different types of greens in its place. Tonight I’m using baby arugula and spinach. I’m sure it will be close to your recipe, but it definitely won’t be as good without the escarole.
I like to add shells ( medium size) to my beans and greens 😊 I make them exactly like yours.
I made this recipe, I added loose Italian sausage. Delicious
This is wonderful! I didn’t have anchovy but added some chopped ham I had left over from Easter. I also drained and rinsed the beans and used low sodium chicken broth.

I love this. I make it 2-3x/year and ALWAYS as alternative to the collards with ham hocks and black eyed peas for New Year’s Day that are popular where I live. I cannot find escarole so I use dinosaur kale or mustard greens instead). I still serve it with fried cornbread (probably should use focaccia instead)
Made it many, many times. Perfect recipe for beans and greens, and pretty fast and easy. Eat with a crusty bread. Yummy!
Delicious! So quick and easy to make! I use escarole when I have it and have substituted Swiss Chard when I don't.
